value_domain: Year-to-date dollar amount of allowances reported in an STP pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Allowances
variable_description: The allowances an employer paid this person, reported apart from ordinary pay. Allowances cover work-related costs or conditions, and the ATO separates them from money paid back against receipts: "Reimbursements should not be reported through STP." The basis of the column moves at the phase change, because "In Phase 1 reporting, some allowances are reported separately, and some are reported as part of Gross. This has changed for STP Phase 2."
value_definition: A dollar amount reported in a pay event for one payee under one payer, cumulative for the financial year to the date of the event rather than the value of that single pay.
limitation: It is not the cost of the person's work-related expenses. Overtime meal and travel allowances up to the ATO reasonable amount need not be reported at all, so the smaller allowances are missing; living away from home allowance fringe benefits are excluded; and the set of allowances inside the total widens once an employer moves to Phase 2.
rationale: The allowances page in the STP guidelines defines what an employer must and must not report as an allowance, and states the Phase 1 to Phase 2 change that breaks the series.
evidence_quote: In Phase 1 reporting, some allowances are reported separately, and some are reported as part of Gross. This has changed for STP Phase 2.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name 'Allowance Income Total Amount - Event payment' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say what counts as an allowance or that the definition changed mid-series.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum A payment on termination
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out on termination that falls into the lump sum A category, which is taxed at a concessional flat rate rather than as ordinary pay. The ATO limits it to "unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993", holiday pay and other leave-related payments that accrued before 18 August 1993, and post-1993 leave paid in connection with a genuine redundancy, an early retirement scheme or the invalidity segment of a termination payment. The type code column beside it says which of those two situations applies.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer, reported apart from gross pay and cumulative to the date of the pay event within the financial year.
limitation: It is not all unused leave paid on termination. Leave that accrued after 17 August 1993 and was paid on an ordinary resignation goes into gross pay instead, so the column captures old accruals and redundancy-linked leave only, and a nil value in a genuine termination is normal rather than a gap.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define the four lump sum types in the ATO's own words, and the STP pay event carries the same lump sum categories as the payment summary it replaced.
evidence_quote: unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which accrual periods fall into lump sum A or why the rest of unused leave is missing.

value_domain: Lump sum A type code, R or T
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: A one-letter code saying why the lump sum A on the same row was paid, which sets the rate of withholding on it. The ATO gives two valid values: "R - if the payment was made for a genuine redundancy, invalidity or under an early retirement scheme" and "T - if the payment was made for any other reason." The code is only completed where there is a lump sum A amount: "If there is no amount included at Lump sum A, do not complete the 'Type' box."
value_definition: A single character from a closed pair, R or T, attached to the lump sum A amount on the same record and blank when that amount is absent.
limitation: A code of T does not mean the person resigned. It is the residual for every reason other than redundancy, invalidity and early retirement, so dismissal, the end of a fixed term and a voluntary quit all sit inside it. The code also describes the lump sum only, not the termination, so it cannot be read as a reason-for-leaving field for the job.
rationale: The payment summary instructions publish both codes with their meanings and the rule for when the box is left blank, which is exactly the domain of this column.
evidence_quote: R - if the payment was made for a genuine redundancy, invalidity or under an early retirement scheme. T - if the payment was made for any other reason.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the field name 'Annual Long Service Leave Unused Lump Sum A Code' and the generic no-value-list sentence, so the two-value domain was never stated.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum B payment on termination
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused long service leave paid out on termination that accrued in the oldest tax era. The ATO defines lump sum B as "Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978", which is why it is reported apart from both gross pay and lump sum A. Anything accrued after that date is reported at lump sum A or inside gross pay depending on when it accrued and why it was paid.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer, covering long service leave entitlements earned before 16 August 1978 and reported outside gross pay.
limitation: It is a vanishing category rather than a live measure: only a person with continuous service since the 1970s can have any, so an overwhelmingly nil column is the expected result and a non-nil value marks extreme tenure rather than a large payout. It does not indicate how much long service leave the person actually took or accrued in total.
rationale: The payment summary instructions give the accrual cut-off that defines lump sum B and separate it from the other three lump sum types.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished lump sum B from lump sum A.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum D payment, tax-free redundancy component
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The part of a redundancy payout that is not taxed at all, reported apart from every other amount on the row. The ATO defines lump sum D as "The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment", which is capped by a base amount and a per-year-of-service amount that both change each year. It is the only lump sum type the STP guidelines leave out of the employer's gross total.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer that is non-assessable, non-exempt income, so no withholding attaches to it and it is not part of the person's taxable income.
limitation: The column name refers to unused leave, but a lump sum D is not a leave payment: it is the tax-free slice of a redundancy or early retirement payout. Because the tax-free cap rises each year, an amount here is bounded by the year's cap rather than by the size of the settlement, so it understates redundancy generosity for long-serving and highly paid workers.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define lump sum D directly, and the STP guidelines' employer-totals table confirms it is the one lump sum type excluded from the gross total.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the leave-flavoured payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, which actively misled: nothing said lump sum D is a redundancy component and not leave.

value_domain: Dollar amount of a lump sum E payment, back pay for an earlier year
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Back pay for work done more than a year earlier, kept apart so the payee can claim the lump sum E tax offset. The ATO defines it as "Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments". Back pay that accrued within the last twelve months is not reported here; it goes to whichever payment type it would have been paid as at the time.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payee under one payer, covering arrears that relate to an earlier income year rather than to the current pay period.
limitation: The category narrows across the phase change: under Phase 2 a return to work payment is reported as lump sum W instead, and back pay below the lump sum E threshold is reported as the payment type it matches, so a fall in this column after an employer transitions is a reporting rule and not a fall in arrears paid. It also says nothing about which year the arrears relate to.
rationale: The payment summary instructions define lump sum E, and the STP Phase 2 quick reference guide shows return to work payments moving to lump sum W and small back payments moving to the matching payment type.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it neither named the twelve-month rule nor warned about the Phase 2 change.

value_domain: Year and month of the payee's date of birth, ABS derived
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The payee's date of birth reduced by the ABS to a month and a year. The ABS treats month and year of birth as a jobholder characteristic on STP data, drawn from the ATO Client Register and otherwise derived from the payroll record, and it holds the value still once set: "the month and year of birth variable is held constant", while age "continues to be updated at the start of a jobholder's birth month each year". Age at a pay event has to be worked out against the pay dates on the same row.
value_definition: A year and month pair with no day component, constant for a payee across their pay events, and derived by the ABS rather than reported as such by the employer.
limitation: It cannot place a person either side of an age threshold that falls on a birthday, which is the point at which superannuation, minimum wage and tax settings change. Because the value is held constant once assigned, a later correction to the underlying record does not necessarily flow through, so the column should be checked against the spine rather than treated as the authority.
rationale: The ABS methodology names a month and year of birth variable on STP-based payroll data, says where the characteristic comes from and states that it is held constant, but it documents the payroll jobs product rather than this PLIDA column, so the mapping is inferred.
evidence_quote: While the month and year of birth variable is held constant, the jobholder's age (as derived from month and year of birth) continues to be updated at the start of a jobholder's birth month each year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Month and year of payee's DOB' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said who derives the value or that the day is not carried.

value_domain: ABS confidentialised identifier for the employing business
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The employer on a pay event, held as an ABS-issued confidentialised business identifier rather than an ABN. The ABS explains the underlying pipeline: it "receives selected employer and employee level data from the ATO STP system, which are combined with employer and jobholder characteristics from the ABS Business Register and ATO Client Register", and the business identifier is what carries industry and size onto a payroll record. On a contractor row the contractor's own business identifier sits in a separate column.
value_definition: An opaque identifier for a business unit, stable across pay events within an extract, and the key that joins a pay event to business characteristics rather than a readable ABN.
limitation: It is not a workplace and not an enterprise group. A single identifier can cover a national employer with branches in every state, so it cannot locate where the work was done, and business restructures create new identifiers that break an employer series without any change in the underlying operation.
rationale: The ABS methodology documents the STP-to-ABS pipeline and the use of the Business Register to attach employer characteristics, but the construction of the confidentialised identifier itself is not published, so the reading is inferred.
evidence_quote: The ABS receives selected employer and employee level data from the ATO STP system, which are combined with employer and jobholder characteristics from the ABS Business Register and ATO Client Register.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'ABS Derived confidentialised business identifier' and the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing said what the identifier is for or what it cannot distinguish.

value_domain: ATO PAYG withholding branch number for the employer
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section C: Payer details
variable_description: The withholding branch the employer reported the pay under, which splits one ABN into separate tax registrations. The ATO explains the arrangement in the payer details of its payment summaries: "If a business has one ABN but multiple branches, each branch may have an individual branch number." It is a tax administration division chosen by the business, so it exists only where the business registered branches with the ATO.
value_definition: A short numeric code attached to the payer on a pay event, present only for businesses that hold more than one PAYG withholding registration under one ABN, and blank otherwise.
limitation: A branch is not a site, a state or a division of operations, so it cannot stand in for workplace geography. Most employers have no branch at all, and a business that reorganises its registrations can renumber branches, which splits or merges an employer series built on ABN plus branch without anything changing on the ground.
rationale: The ATO's payer details instruction defines the branch number in the same terms the custodian's label uses, and the same identifier is carried on the STP pay event.
evidence_quote: If a business has one ABN but multiple branches, each branch may have an individual branch number.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label about sub-dividing activities and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not warn that a branch is a tax registration and not a location.

value_domain: ABS confidentialised identifier for the contractor's own business
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
variable_description: The business identifier of the person being paid, present where the payee is a contractor rather than an employee. The ATO sets out when the payer has to supply it: "When you report a payment and withholding for a contractor under the voluntary agreement (VOL) income type, you must provide the contractor's ABN. The contractor's TFN is not required." Where a payee is both a contractor and an employee under the same payroll identifier in a year, the payer reports both the ABN and the TFN.
value_definition: An opaque business identifier for the payee's own enterprise, populated only on contractor arrangements, and confidentialised by the ABS in the same way as the employer identifier.
limitation: A value here identifies the payee's business, not the payer's, so joining it to business characteristics describes the contractor rather than the hirer. It is also not a general contractor flag: labour hire and other specified payments identify the payee by tax file number instead, so those rows carry nothing here even though the payee is a contractor.
rationale: The guidelines state which income type requires the contractor's ABN and how a mixed contractor-and-employee case is reported, which is what fixes the meaning of the column and its blanks.
evidence_quote: When you report a payment and withholding for a contractor under the voluntary agreement (VOL) income type, you must provide the contractor's ABN. The contractor's TFN is not required.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Contractor Client Identifier - ABS Derived confidentialised business identifier' with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said which side of the payment the identifier belongs to.

value_domain: Derived end date of the pay period covered by an STP pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Definition of terms
variable_description: The last day of the period the pay event covers, worked out rather than reported by the employer. The event itself is anchored to the payment: a pay event is "the file generated by an STP-enabled software or solution" that "must be lodged to us on, or before, the payment date when an employer makes a payment to an employee or payee". The derived end date lets a payment be placed against the weeks worked instead of the day the money moved, which is what the payment date column gives.
value_definition: A calendar date marking the close of the pay period. It pairs with the derived start date on the same row, and the two together bound the period the reported amounts relate to.
limitation: It is not an employment date. A pay period ending does not mean the job ended, which is what the payer-payee cessation date records, and because the date is derived it can be modelled from a pay cycle where the payroll file carried no period. Overlapping and out-of-sequence periods occur when an employer corrects earlier reporting.
rationale: The ATO defines the pay event and its relationship to the payment date, but the derivation of the pay period bounds is an ABS treatment that is not documented on a fetchable page, so the reading rests on the field name and the neighbouring date columns.
evidence_quote: Pay event - the file generated by an STP-enabled software or solution. This file must be lodged to us on, or before, the payment date when an employer makes a payment to an employee or payee that is subject to withholding.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Derived end date for a pay event' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not distinguish the pay period from the payment date or from the end of the job.

value_domain: Derived start date of the pay period covered by an STP pay event
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The first day of the period the pay event covers, worked out rather than reported by the employer. Pay cycles differ between employers: the ABS notes that STP "transactions reported each week are generally for payments of wages and salaries for a defined pay cycle period" and that submissions "vary from employer to employer based on pay cycle frequency". The start date is what makes a weekly, fortnightly and monthly payer comparable on a time basis.
value_definition: A calendar date marking the opening of the pay period, paired with the derived end date on the same row, and expressed in the same daily resolution as the payment date.
limitation: It is not the date the job started, which the payer-payee commencement date carries and which can be decades earlier. A long gap between this date and the previous event's end date can be a change of pay cycle, a correction or a period of unpaid leave, and the column cannot tell those apart.
rationale: The ABS methodology describes the pay cycle periods STP transactions carry and the calendarisation that uses the start and end date of the payment period, but the derived start date itself is an ABS construction that is not published field by field.
evidence_quote: Transactions reported each week are generally for payments of wages and salaries for a defined pay cycle period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Derived start date for a pay event' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not separate the pay period from the start of employment.

value_domain: True or false flag marking a record with a holding identifier
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
variable_description: A true or false marker showing that the payee identifier on the row is a stand-in rather than a real one. Payroll reporting produces these cases by design: "You must provide either a TFN or Australian business number (ABN) for each payee included in your STP report. If you have not been provided with the employee's TFN you must use the TFN exemption codes." A row flagged true still carries pay amounts, but the person behind it cannot be linked to the spine with confidence.
value_definition: A two-state flag, true or false, applied at the record level and independent of the amounts reported on the same row.
limitation: It does not say why the identifier is a stand-in, so a new starter whose tax file number declaration has not yet come through, a payee who declined to quote one and a payroll error all look the same. Dropping flagged rows removes real wages from an employer's total, and keeping them risks attaching one person's pay to another, so the choice has to be made deliberately rather than by default.
rationale: The ATO documents the exemption codes that stand in for a missing tax file number, which is the situation this flag most plausibly marks, but no published page defines the PLIDA flag itself.
evidence_quote: If you have not been provided with the employee's TFN you must use the TFN exemption codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Dummy flag. Value of True or False' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it stated the shape of the field and nothing about what it marks.

value_domain: Identifier for one payee and payer pairing, that is, one payroll job
value_source: ABS, Payroll Jobs methodology, week ending 15 March 2025
variable_description: The job, in the sense the ABS uses for payroll statistics: one person paid by one employer. The ABS definition is direct - "A payroll job is a relationship between an employee and their employer where the employee is paid through STP-enabled payroll or accounting software" - and this key is what makes that relationship countable across pay events. The sequence key on the same row goes finer, adding the payroll identifier, branch number and business management software identifier.
value_definition: An encrypted identifier that is constant for a payee and payer combination and repeats across every pay event for that relationship in the extract.
limitation: Counting keys counts relationships, not people and not job starts. One person holding two jobs generates two keys, a person rehired by the same employer can keep the same key across a break, and a person who moves to a related entity with a different business identifier gets a new key even though the work did not change.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines a payroll job in exactly the payee-and-payer terms the custodian uses for this key, and that definition governs how the column behaves in counts.
evidence_quote: A payroll job is a relationship between an employee and their employer where the employee is paid through STP-enabled payroll or accounting software.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Key unique to a payee-payer combination' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never connected the key to the payroll job concept or warned how it behaves in counts.

value_domain: Date an employment termination payment was made
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The day the employer actually paid the termination payment. The ATO instruction is the plainest possible: "Show the date you made the payment to the payee." It is the date the money moved, which is what determines the income year the payment is taxed in and which cap applies to it.
value_definition: A calendar date on an employment termination payment record, one per payment type reported, since a separate record is required for each code.
limitation: It is not the date employment ended. A termination payment can follow the last day of work by weeks or months, and can be paid in instalments that fall in different financial years, which is why the codes for a payment continuing an earlier year's entitlement exist. The end of the job sits in the payer-payee cessation date on the pay event table.
rationale: The ATO's payment details instruction defines the date field on the termination payment record, and the same field is carried through STP reporting of termination payments.
evidence_quote: Show the date you made the payment to the payee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Date Employment Termination Payment was paid' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not warn that this is a payment date rather than a termination date.

value_domain: Employment termination payment code, life benefit or death benefit
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Employment termination payment (ETP) codes
variable_description: A one-letter code putting the termination payment into a tax category, which decides the cap and the rate applied to it. The first split is who the payment is for: "A life benefit ETP is a lump sum payment made to a living employee in consequence of their employment being terminated", and codes for a death benefit are used "If you are paying the ETP to a person because of another person's death". A second split marks payments continuing an entitlement partly paid in an earlier income year for the same termination.
value_definition: A single letter drawn from the life benefit codes and the death benefit codes, with one code per record, since a payer reporting more than one type has to report each separately.
limitation: The code does not say why the job ended. It classifies the payment for tax, so the choice between the two life benefit codes turns on which cap applies rather than on redundancy against resignation, and a person made redundant can appear under either depending on what the payment consists of. Codes marking a continuing entitlement also describe the payment's history, not the current year's separation.
rationale: The ATO's code guidance defines the life benefit and death benefit branches and the earlier-year rule, which are the distinctions this column encodes.
evidence_quote: A life benefit ETP is a lump sum payment made to a living employee in consequence of their employment being terminated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's note that value domain information sits below the data item list, with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it gave the reader no way to read the codes.

value_domain: Dollar amount, tax-free component of an employment termination payment
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The part of a termination payment that is not taxed, which is narrow and historical in origin. The ATO says "The tax-free component consists of the: pre-July 1983 segment" and the "invalidity segment", so it reflects very long service or a payment made because the person could no longer work. It is also optional on the form: "You do not have to complete this field."
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount that is non-assessable, non-exempt income, so no withholding attaches to it and it stays outside the payer's gross total.
limitation: A blank is not evidence that the whole payment was taxable, because the payer is not required to complete the field, so the split between the two components on a row can be incomplete. It is also not the same concept as the tax-free redundancy lump sum on the pay event table, which is reported under a lump sum type rather than as part of a termination payment.
rationale: The payment details instruction defines the two segments that make up the tax-free component and states that completing the field is optional, which governs how a blank should be read.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component consists of the: pre-July 1983 segment, invalidity segment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about non-assessable non-exempt income with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say what the component consists of or that the field is optional.

value_domain: Dollar amount of PAYG withholding on an employment termination payment
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Tax the employer held back from the termination payment and sent to the ATO. The instruction is to "Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars", covering the whole payment reported on that record. Withholding on a termination payment follows its own tax table, so the rate is not the person's marginal rate and not the rate applied to their ordinary pay.
value_definition: A whole-dollar withholding amount attached to one termination payment record, and part of the payer's PAYG withholding total rather than its gross payment total.
limitation: Withholding is not tax paid. The caps that govern how much of a termination payment is concessionally taxed are applied by the ATO across the person's year, so an assessment can refund or add to this amount, and the ratio of this column to the taxable component is not an effective tax rate.
rationale: The payment details instruction defines the withholding field on the termination payment record, and the STP guidelines put the same amount into the payer's withholding total rather than the gross total.
evidence_quote: Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about tax withheld under the Pay As You Go arrangement with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not separate withholding from final tax.

value_domain: Dollar amount, taxable component of an employment termination payment
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - employment termination payment (from 1 July 2012), Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The assessable part of a termination payment. The ATO defines it as a residual: "Include the total of the payment, less the tax-free component." A death benefit paid to a dependant is reported differently, because for those payments the payer must "only include the amount over the ETP cap in the taxable component". A payee with more than one type of termination payment has more than one record, since each code is reported separately.
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable amount for one payment and one code, included in the payer's gross total and paired with the tax-free component on the same record.
limitation: It understates the payment for a death benefit to a dependant, where everything under the cap is reported as nothing at all, so summing the column across payees is not the value of termination payments made. Nor is it the whole payout on separation: unused leave paid at the same time is reported on the pay event table under the lump sum types, not here.
rationale: The payment details instruction defines the taxable component as the payment less the tax-free component and states the different treatment of a dependant's death benefit, which is where the column stops being additive.
evidence_quote: For death benefit ETP's paid to a dependant of the deceased, only include the amount over the ETP cap in the taxable component.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's note about a repeating array of amounts with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say how the component is worked out or where it is deliberately understated.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross foreign employment income in a pay event
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - foreign employment, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Pay an Australian tax resident earned working overseas, where that income is assessable in Australia. The ATO says "The gross payments amount is the assessable foreign employment income" and adds that on this reporting stream "allowances must be included in Gross payments", unlike the domestic gross column, where allowances sit separately. Foreign service that qualifies as exempt is reported elsewhere and is not part of this amount.
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars for one payee, payer and income type, cumulative for the financial year at the time of the pay event.
limitation: It is not all money earned abroad. Exempt foreign earnings are excluded, and payments made by a foreign employer with no Australian payroll never enter STP at all, so the column measures foreign work paid through an Australian payroll. Because allowances are folded in here but not in domestic gross, the two gross columns are not on the same basis.
rationale: The foreign employment payment summary defines the gross figure as assessable foreign employment income and states the allowance treatment, and the STP income types page confirms the foreign employment income type carries the same concept.
evidence_quote: The gross payments amount is the assessable foreign employment income. For this payment summary it also includes total allowances.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is assessable income only or that allowances are inside it.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross income for work in the Joint Petroleum Development Area
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types; type letter from ATO, PAYG payment summary - foreign employment, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Gross pay for work done in the Timor Sea joint petroleum area, which was taxed under its own treaty arrangements. The foreign employment payment summary marks it with a distinct type - "J - income earned for work conducted in the Joint Petroleum Development Area (JPDA)" - and the ATO now treats the category as closed: "You can only use this income type to make amendments to your STP reporting for the 2019-20 or earlier financial years, because the tax arrangements relating to the JPDA changed in 2019."
value_definition: A dollar amount in Australian dollars, cumulative for the financial year, reported separately from other foreign employment income for the same payee.
limitation: After 2019-20 a non-zero value is an amendment to an earlier year rather than new work in the area, so a time series built on payment date will attribute old activity to the wrong year. The column also cannot be used to count offshore petroleum workers, since employees of foreign operators paid outside an Australian payroll are absent.
rationale: The STP income types page states when the joint petroleum area income type may still be used and why it closed, and the foreign employment payment summary defines the type letter for the same concept.
evidence_quote: You can only use this income type to make amendments to your STP reporting for the 2019-20 or earlier financial years, because the tax arrangements relating to the JPDA changed in 2019.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, so a reader could not tell what the area is or that the category effectively ended in 2019.

value_domain: Year-to-date PAYG withholding on Joint Petroleum Development Area income
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid
variable_description: Australian tax withheld from pay for work in the joint petroleum area, held apart from withholding on every other income type. The ATO requires the split: "You must include separate YTD amounts you have withheld from each income type (and for income types that require a country code, for each combination of income type and country code)." Like the gross column beside it, the field only carries new activity up to 2019-20, after which it takes amendments.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount of withholding for one payee, payer and income type within the financial year, paired with the gross column for the same income type.
limitation: The reading as a withholding total is inferred from the sibling columns for labour hire and voluntary agreement, which name PAYG withholding explicitly, rather than from a published field definition, so an alternative reading as a second income total cannot be ruled out. It is in any case withholding rather than tax assessed, and the offshore treaty arrangements mean the rate is not comparable with domestic withholding.
rationale: The ATO requires withholding to be reported as a separate year-to-date amount for each income type, which is the pattern the gross and total pairs on this table follow, but no published page names this specific field.
evidence_quote: You must include separate YTD amounts you have withheld from each income type (and for income types that require a country code, for each combination of income type and country code).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, which left it indistinguishable from the gross column for the same income type.

value_domain: Year-to-date PAYG withholding on foreign employment income, net of foreign tax
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid
variable_description: Australian withholding on foreign employment income after credit is given for tax paid overseas. The rule is specific to this income type: "If you are reporting amounts you have withheld from payments you are reporting against the FEI income type, you must only report the residual amount withheld after the deduction of foreign tax paid." That makes the figure smaller than withholding on the same wage earned in Australia, by the amount of foreign tax on the row beside it.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount of Australian withholding for one payee and payer within the financial year, reduced by the foreign tax the employer paid or expects to pay.
limitation: The mapping of this field to the residual withholding rests on the label wording read against the ATO's netting rule rather than on a published field list, so it could instead be the gross withholding before credit. Either way it cannot be added to withholding on other income types to get the person's Australian tax, because the foreign tax deducted here is claimed separately in their return.
rationale: The guidelines set out a netting rule that applies only to foreign employment income withholding, which matches a field whose name combines a tax credit with an amount withheld.
evidence_quote: If you are reporting amounts you have withheld from payments you are reporting against the FEI income type, you must only report the residual amount withheld after the deduction of foreign tax paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say the amount is netted against foreign tax or how it differs from the foreign tax column.

value_domain: Year-to-date foreign tax paid on foreign employment income
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid
variable_description: Tax on the person's overseas earnings that went to a foreign government rather than to the ATO. The employer "must report the amount of foreign tax that you have paid or are required to pay to a foreign government or authority", and must do so in the same Australian financial year as the payment even if the foreign tax is settled later. "The amount you report must be in Australian dollars."
value_definition: A cumulative Australian-dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, converted from the foreign currency, and separate from Australian withholding.
limitation: It can be an estimate rather than a settled liability, because an employer that does not know the foreign tax by payday may report zero or an estimate and correct it at finalisation, so mid-year values are unreliable. The mapping of this field name to foreign tax paid is inferred from the label and the ATO's field set rather than from a published data dictionary.
rationale: The guidelines define a foreign tax paid amount that sits alongside foreign employment income withholding, and state both the currency rule and the estimation allowance that shape how the column behaves.
evidence_quote: If you do not know the amount of foreign tax on or before each payday, then you can report zero or estimate the amount of foreign tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say whose tax this is or that the value may be an estimate.

value_domain: Year-to-date PAYG withholding total for foreign employment income
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid
variable_description: The withholding total the employer reported against the foreign employment income type. Income-type totals of this kind exist because the ATO requires the split: "You must report the amounts you withhold from payments you make to employees. You must include separate YTD amounts you have withheld from each income type." It pairs with the gross foreign employment income column on the same row.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee, payer and income type within the financial year, reported apart from the withholding totals for salary and wages and for the other income types.
limitation: The reading rests on the sibling columns for labour hire and voluntary agreement, which spell out PAYG withholding in their labels, so a reading as a second measure of foreign employment income cannot be excluded and the column should be checked against the gross column before use. It is also not comparable with domestic withholding, because foreign employment withholding is reported after credit for foreign tax.
rationale: The guidelines establish per-income-type withholding totals as a required part of every STP report, which is the pattern the paired gross and total columns on this table follow.
evidence_quote: You must report the amounts you withhold from payments you make to employees. You must include separate YTD amounts you have withheld from each income type.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence, so it read as a duplicate of the gross foreign employment income column.

value_domain: Year-to-date exempt foreign employment income in a pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Exempt foreign employment income
variable_description: Overseas earnings that are exempt from Australian tax, reported for the record rather than for withholding. The ATO says that where "the employee's foreign service qualifies as exempt foreign income, it is not subject to withholding and must be reported in STP Phase 2 against the income type SAW as exempt foreign income". The column has no history before that: "This is a new reporting requirement for STP Phase 2. It was not required to be reported under previous reporting phases such as STP Phase 1 or payment summaries."
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, reported after salary sacrifice rather than before it, which is the exception to the Phase 2 pre-sacrifice rule.
limitation: A nil before an employer moved to Phase 2 reflects the reporting rules and not an absence of exempt foreign service, so the column cannot be used for a series that spans the transition. Because it is reported after sacrifice while every other gross column is reported before it, adding it to those columns mixes two bases.
rationale: The dedicated guidelines page states when the amount must be reported, that it carries no withholding, that it is new in Phase 2, and that it is the one post-sacrifice amount.
evidence_quote: This is a new reporting requirement for STP Phase 2. It was not required to be reported under previous reporting phases such as STP Phase 1 or payment summaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the column is empty by design for the earlier years of the asset.

value_domain: Year-to-date workplace giving donations deducted from pay
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Money the employer took out of this person's pay and passed to a charity on their behalf. The ATO describes the field as amounts "you paid to deductible gift recipients on behalf of your payee", and is explicit that the money is still the person's wage: "You must include these amounts in Gross payments." The employer may reduce withholding to reflect the donation, which is the point of running giving through the payroll.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, covering donations to endorsed deductible gift recipients arranged through the payroll.
limitation: It is a subtotal of gross pay, not an addition to it, so adding the two counts the donation twice. It also captures only giving routed through an employer, so a person who donates directly to the same charity shows nothing here, and the column is a measure of a payroll arrangement rather than of generosity.
rationale: The payment summary instruction defines the workplace giving field and states its relationship to gross payments, which is the trap the column sets for anyone building an income measure.
evidence_quote: Show amounts you paid to deductible gift recipients on behalf of your payee here.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Payee workplace giving amount - Event payment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is inside gross pay.

value_domain: Year-to-date payments from a Community Development Employment Projects wages grant
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Wages paid to a worker out of a Community Development Employment Projects grant, kept apart from ordinary pay because they were taxed differently. The ATO defines the field as "the total you have paid to your worker/payee from a CDEP wages grant" and adds "Do not include this amount in gross payments." The programme was an Indigenous employment scheme in which a community organisation paid participants from grant money rather than from its own revenue.
value_definition: A cumulative whole-dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, reported separately from gross payments and from allowances.
limitation: The category has no successor once an employer moves to Phase 2 reporting, whose income type list carries no equivalent, so a nil in the later years of the asset is a reporting rule rather than a change in what people were paid. It also measures grant money passing through an organisation, so it is not part of that organisation's own wage bill and should not be read as employer-funded employment.
rationale: The payment summary instruction defines the field in the ATO's own words and states its exclusion from gross payments; the Phase 2 income types page has no corresponding category, which fixes the end of the series.
evidence_quote: This is the total you have paid to your worker/payee from a CDEP wages grant. You must show this amount in whole dollars. Do not include this amount in gross payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name with the abbreviation spelt out and nothing more, plus the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say what the programme was or when the reporting stopped.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross salary and wages in a pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross
variable_description: The main pay figure on a pay event, and the one whose meaning narrows sharply partway through the asset. Under Phase 2, "Instead of reporting a single gross amount, you must separately report: gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W, salary sacrifice", and what stays behind is tightly drawn: "Only pre-sacrifice amounts that are classified as ordinary time earnings (OTE) should be included as gross." Under Phase 1 the same column carried most of the pay packet.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee, payer and income type within the financial year, covering ordinary hours, casual loading, shift penalties and other ordinary time earnings once Phase 2 applies.
limitation: The column is not a consistent series. A fall at the date an employer transitions is a change of definition, not a pay cut, because leave, overtime, bonuses and directors' fees move out and pre-sacrifice reporting moves in. Rebuilding total pay after the change means adding the sibling columns back, and adding them before the change double counts.
rationale: The disaggregation page states what gross became under Phase 2 and lists the amounts that were pulled out of it, which is the single most important fact about this column's comparability over time.
evidence_quote: Instead of reporting a single gross amount, you must separately report: gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W, salary sacrifice.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Gross amount of salary & wages income - Event payment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no warning that the definition of gross changed mid-series.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross payments under a labour hire arrangement
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: Payments a labour hire firm made to a worker it placed with a client, where the worker is not the firm's employee. The ATO defines the income type as payments "by a labour hire firm that arranges for persons to perform work or services, or performances, directly for their clients", and draws the line at employment: "This income type relates to contractors only. It doesn't include amounts paid to employees of labour hire firms." Withholding on these payments is reported in the labour hire total on the same row.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, reported apart from salary and wages and from the other contractor income types.
limitation: It does not identify labour hire employment. Workers employed by the firm are reported as salary and wages, so a labour hire business shows both kinds of row and this column picks up only the contracting side. It also names the hiring firm, not the client business the person actually worked at, so it cannot be used to place the work in an industry.
rationale: The income types page defines the labour hire income type and states that it excludes employees, which is the distinction that decides what the column counts.
evidence_quote: Use this income type to report payments by a labour hire firm that arranges for persons to perform work or services, or performances, directly for their clients.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the column covers contractors only or that the client business is invisible.

value_domain: Year-to-date residual income amount in a pay event
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross
variable_description: A residual pay amount that does not belong to any of the named income or payment types on the same row. STP reporting is built around a closed set of categories - gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W and salary sacrifice under Phase 2, and the payment summary types under Phase 1 - and payroll systems need somewhere to put money that does not fit one of them. The column should be read against the named amounts beside it, not on its own.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, holding reported pay that is not attributed to a named category.
limitation: There is no published label of this name, so what falls into it depends on the payroll product and on the reporting phase, which makes it unsafe to compare between employers or over time. A large value is more likely to indicate a mapping problem in a payroll system than a real category of pay.
rationale: The disaggregation page fixes the closed set of reportable payment types, which is the context that makes a residual field intelligible, but no ATO page defines a field with this name.
evidence_quote: STP requires payment types to be disaggregated so that we can identify the sorts of amounts your employees are paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Income Other Amount - Event payment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and stating openly that the field is a residual with no published definition is more useful than repeating the label.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross payments under a voluntary agreement for PAYG withholding
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: Payments to an independent contractor who agreed with the payer that tax should be withheld from their invoices. The ATO defines the income type as payments "subject to a voluntary agreement for PAYG withholding" and states that it "relates to contractors that have a voluntary agreement in place. Don't use this income type to report amounts paid to employees." A row of this kind identifies the payee by their own business number rather than by tax file number.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, being the contract payments covered by the agreement, with the matching withholding in the voluntary agreement total.
limitation: A row here is not employment, so counting it as a job overstates the employed workforce. The agreement is entirely optional between the two parties, so most contracting income never reaches STP at all and the column is a lower bound on contracting rather than a measure of it.
rationale: The income types page defines the voluntary agreement income type and says it applies to contractors and not employees, and the business and personal services payment summary describes the underlying agreement.
evidence_quote: Use this income type to report payments that are subject to a voluntary agreement for PAYG withholding. This income type relates to contractors that have a voluntary agreement in place.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the payee is a contractor or that the arrangement is voluntary.

value_domain: Year-to-date gross pay reported under the working holiday maker income type
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: Pay earned by someone on a working holiday visa, kept separate because it is taxed on its own scale. The ATO defines the income type as income "a person has earned while they were a working holiday maker", meaning "a temporary visitor to Australia holding a subclass 417 (working holiday) or subclass 462 (work and holiday) visa". Employers must also report a country code with it, being the person's country of nationality on that visa.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount for one payee, payer and income type within the financial year, with the matching withholding reported in the working holiday maker total.
limitation: It records how the employer withheld, not the person's visa on any given day. When a visa ends mid-year the employer moves later pay to salary and wages, so the split of one person's year between the two columns is an approximate date of visa change; and an employer who is not registered to employ working holiday makers may report the income the wrong way, which shifts pay out of this column without the worker changing.
rationale: The income types page defines the working holiday maker income type by visa subclass and explains the mid-year switch with a worked example, which is what governs how the column behaves for a person whose status changes.
evidence_quote: This income type tells us about the income a person has earned while they were a working holiday maker. Use this income type when you're making payments to a person that is a working holiday maker.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the payroll field name and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it named no visa subclass and gave no warning about mid-year switching.

value_domain: Year-to-date PAYG withholding on labour hire payments
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - business and personal services income
variable_description: Tax the labour hire firm withheld from payments to a worker it placed with a client. The obligation is on the firm, not the client: "If you provide workers for other businesses under a labour-hire arrangement, you must withhold amounts from payments you make to the individual workers and send these amounts to us." It is reported against the labour hire income type, so it pairs with the labour hire gross column and not with the salary and wages withholding total.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount of withholding for one payee, payer and income type within the financial year, forming part of the payer's total PAYG withholding.
limitation: It is withholding, not the worker's tax. Labour hire withholding follows the payer's obligation rather than the worker's circumstances, and the worker's own assessment settles the position, so the ratio of this column to labour hire gross is not an effective tax rate. Workers under a voluntary agreement are withheld from under a different arrangement and appear in a different total.
rationale: The business and personal services payment summary states the labour hire withholding obligation, and the STP guidelines require withholding to be reported separately for each income type, which is what this total is.
evidence_quote: If you provide workers for other businesses under a labour-hire arrangement, you must withhold amounts from payments you make to the individual workers and send these amounts to us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Labour Hire Total PAYGW Amount - Event payment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it left the abbreviation unexpanded and did not distinguish withholding from tax.

value_domain: Flag marking the last event for a job in the financial year
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Definition of terms
variable_description: A flag picking out the last event reported for a job in a financial year, which is the one to keep because STP amounts are cumulative. The ATO describes the closing declaration as finalisation, "when an employer must make a declaration to us that they have provided all the information for each employee for a financial year", and it describes the income statement a person sees as containing "the latest year to date (YTD) STP data reported by employers". Filtering to the flagged row gives one final position per job instead of a running total repeated across events.
value_definition: A two-state flag on an event record, true on the record with the latest payroll run timestamp for a job within the financial year and false on all earlier records for the same job.
limitation: The flagged row is the last one reported, not necessarily a finalised one, so a job whose employer never lodged a finalisation still carries a flagged event that may be incomplete. Because the flag is assigned within a financial year, a job spanning two years has one flagged record in each, and a person who changed employers has one in each job.
rationale: The ATO defines finalisation and the year-to-date basis of STP data, which is what makes a latest-record flag meaningful, but the flag itself is a PLIDA construction with no published definition.
evidence_quote: Income statement - the equivalent of an employer-issued payment summary. It contains the latest year to date (YTD) STP data reported by employers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Latest event flag - latest transaction in the FY sorted by payroll run timestamp' with the generic no-value-list sentence, so it never said why the flag matters, which is that the amounts are cumulative and must not be summed.

value_domain: ASGS Local Government Area code, 2022 vintage
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the ABS geocoded from the address the employer held for the payee when it lodged this pay event. ABS warns that the boundary is a statistical construction rather than the legal one: Local Government Areas "are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory" and "should only be used for statistical purposes". It is the administrative member of the row's geography set, sitting beside the SA2 and mesh block codes, which are statistical areas built for comparability rather than for local government.
value_definition: A five-digit code: one digit for state or territory and four for the Local Government Area, always ending in zero. ASGS Edition 3 has 567 areas covering the whole country, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes, and the 2022 annual update is the vintage the column name pins.
limitation: It places the worker's home, not the job, so a count of employees by council says nothing about where the work happens. Councils also amalgamate and split, and the ABS retires an identifier when an area is abolished, so a 2022 code cannot be compared with an earlier or later vintage without a correspondence file.
rationale: The custodian's label reads 'Geocoded LGA' and names the 2022 LGA vintage, so the classification is the ABS Local Government Area structure. The ASGS Edition 3 chapter for that structure gives the definition, the coding rule and the count of areas.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the two-word custodian label 'Geocoded LGA' with the value domain inferred from the variable name, and it never said whose address is coded or that the boundary is an approximation.

value_domain: PAYG withholding on other specified payments, year to date (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types
variable_description: Tax withheld year to date from the narrow class of payments STP calls other specified payments, reported under income type OSP. The ATO defines the class by regulation rather than by description: "Use this income type if the payments you are reporting are the specific payments specified by regulation 27 of the Taxation Administration Regulations 2017". The column belongs to the family of per-income-type withholding totals that also holds VA_TOTL_AMT, LABR_HIR_TOTL_AMT and WHM_TOTL_AMT, so it captures withholding rather than the gross payment.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount of PAYG withholding within the financial year, covering only amounts the employer assigned to the other specified payments income type.
limitation: It cannot tell you which regulation 27 payment was made, so the column groups unlike arrangements under one number. A zero is also uninformative: it is the usual state for almost every employer, and it looks the same whether no such payment was made or the payer classified the same payment as ordinary salary and wages.
rationale: The label matches the STP other specified payments income type, whose scope the ATO guidelines define by pointing at regulation 27. The custodian's wording drops the PAYGW that the sibling labour hire, voluntary agreement and working holiday maker labels carry, so the withholding reading comes from the column family rather than from the label itself.
evidence_quote: Use this income type if the payments you are reporting are the specific payments specified by regulation 27 of the Taxation Administration Regulations 2017
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Other Specified Total Amount - Event payment' and inferred a dollar domain from the variable name, so nothing said which payments are specified or by what.

value_domain: Pay day (calendar date)
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Rules of reporting through STP
variable_description: The day the employee was paid, which is the day the whole pay event is anchored to. The ATO ties reporting to it: "The pay day is either the payment date stipulated in the electronic transaction to your financial institution or, if you did not specify a date for payment, the date you intend to make the payment into your employee's bank account." DRVPAYSTARTDATE and DRVPAYENDDATE on the same row bound the pay period the money covers, so the gap between them and this date is the lag between working and being paid.
value_definition: A calendar date. Every dollar amount on the row is a year-to-date total as at this date, so consecutive rows for one payroll stream are cumulative rather than period amounts.
limitation: It dates the payment, not the work or the lodgement. Pay for June work banked on 3 July belongs to the next financial year, an out-of-cycle bonus can arrive on a date of its own, and a report covering this pay day may be lodged later where a concessional arrangement applies.
rationale: The STP reporting rules define the pay day and make it the due date for the report, which is exactly what this column holds.
evidence_quote: The pay day is either the payment date stipulated in the electronic transaction to your financial institution or, if you did not specify a date for payment, the date you intend to make the payment into your employee's bank account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Payment Date' with a calendar-date domain inferred from the name, and gave a reader no way to tell it from the derived pay period dates beside it.

value_domain: Gross payments, year to date (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross
variable_description: Gross pay for this payroll stream, accumulated from the start of the financial year and reported before tax and before deductions. What sits inside the number changed with STP Phase 2: "Instead of reporting a single gross amount, you must separately report: gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W, salary sacrifice." The ATO also narrows what remains: "Only pre-sacrifice amounts that are classified as ordinary time earnings (OTE) should be included as gross."
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount within the financial year. Under Phase 2 it covers ordinary hours, casual loading, shift penalties, piece and daily rates and flexi time, with leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses, directors' fees and sacrificed amounts carried in their own columns.
limitation: The series is not continuous across the monthly tables. Employers moved to Phase 2 reporting from 1 January 2022, and after they did, amounts that had been folded into this one figure moved out to separate columns, so a fall in gross around a payer's transition is a reporting change rather than a pay cut. Differencing consecutive months also fails wherever the payroll identifiers changed, because the count restarts.
rationale: The guidelines' disaggregation chapter is the authority on what employers must and must not include in the gross figure, and it is the change that breaks this column's comparability over the period the monthly tables cover.
evidence_quote: Instead of reporting a single gross amount, you must separately report: gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W, salary sacrifice.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's 'Total amount of gross payments an individual has received' and inferred a dollar domain, so it did not warn that the composition of gross changed part-way through the tables.

value_domain: Employment cessation date
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, When an employee transfers or leaves
variable_description: The day the employer says this job ended, which it must report once the employee leaves. The ATO puts the obligation plainly: "You must report your employee's cessation date when they leave." The date is deliberately not updated by later money, since "If you make another payment to that employee after the cessation date (for example, an eligible termination payment (ETP)), you do not need to update the cessation date", so pay events and ETP rows can carry dates after it. Paired with PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_CMNCMT_DT on the jobs tables, it bounds a spell of employment with one payer.
value_definition: A calendar date, empty while the job continues and while the employer has nothing to report. One employee can hold several of them in a year, one for each payroll stream they left.
limitation: A blank does not mean the person is still working. Where an employer only moves a worker between combinations of ABN and branch, the ATO says to report no cessation at all, so genuine changes of legal employer within a group leave no trace here; and the date says nothing about why the job ended, because the cessation reason the employer reports to the ATO is not carried in this extract.
rationale: The guidelines chapter on employees leaving states the obligation to report a cessation date, the rule against updating it for later payments, and the transfer cases in which no cessation is reported.
evidence_quote: If you make another payment to that employee after the cessation date (for example, an eligible termination payment (ETP)), you do not need to update the cessation date.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the label 'Payer Payee Relationship Cessation Date' with a date domain inferred from the name, and did not say that transfers within a corporate group are reported without a cessation.

value_domain: Employment commencement date
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, How to report employment and tax information through STP Phase 2
variable_description: The start date the employer recognises for this employment relationship, which it must report for every employee in every STP report. It is an industrial date rather than a first-pay date: "Generally, the date you report will be the commencement date that you recognise to meet your industrial obligations", and service with related entities, recognised prior service after a transfer of business, breaks in service and leave without pay can all shift it. Read against PYR_PYE_RLTNSHP_CESTN_DT, it opens the job spell that the cessation date closes.
value_definition: A calendar date, present on every reported employee rather than only on new starters, and repeated unchanged on each pay event for that payroll stream.
limitation: A filled date is not always a real start date. The ATO allows a holding value of 01/01/1800 where the employer does not know when the person started, and requires that same value for a death beneficiary being paid an ETP, so tenure calculated from this column will be absurd for those rows and merely early for anyone whose prior service was recognised.
rationale: The guidelines set out what date to report, the situations that adjust it and the default value to use when it is unknown, which is what a reader needs before treating the column as a start of employment.
evidence_quote: If you don't know your employees' commencement date, you can report a default date of '01/01/1800'.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Payer Payee Relationship Commencement Date' with an inferred date domain and gave no warning about the 01/01/1800 default or recognised prior service.

value_domain: Terminated-before-reporting flag (T or blank)
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, When an employee transfers or leaves
variable_description: A flag marking the case where the job had already finished before the employer first told the ATO about the payer and payee relationship. It exists because a pay event both declares the relationship and reports the money, so a very short engagement, a late first report or a back payment to a former worker can arrive with nothing left to terminate. The cessation date column carries the day the job ended; this column only records that the ending preceded the report.
value_definition: A one-character flag: T where the relationship had ended before it was reported, and blank in every other case, including for employees who are still working and for most people who left.
limitation: It is not a leaver flag. Someone whose job ended after the relationship was reported shows up through the cessation date instead, with this field blank, so counting T values counts a reporting sequence rather than job separations.
rationale: The custodian's own label states the T-or-blank rule, and the guidelines chapter on leaving employees supplies the surrounding obligation to report cessation and the cases in which it is reported late or not at all. The reading of why the flag exists is assembled rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: You must report your employee's cessation date when they leave.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long custodian sentence about setting the field to T, with the value domain inferred from the variable name, and never explained why a relationship would be terminated before it was reported or how the flag differs from the cessation date.

value_domain: Reportable employer super contributions, year to date (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Identify reportable employer super contributions
variable_description: The extra super the employer paid beyond what it was compelled to pay, which the ATO calls reportable employer super contributions. The test is influence: an amount is reportable where "your employee can influence the rate or amount of super you contribute for them" and it is additional to the compulsory contributions required by the super guarantee, an industrial agreement, the fund's rules or the law. The three usual sources are a negotiated salary package, a salary sacrifice arrangement and a pre-tax amount such as a bonus directed into super at the employee's request.
value_definition: A cumulative dollar amount within the financial year. It counts only the contribution above the compulsory minimum, so an employer that agrees to a rate above the super guarantee reports the difference between the two rates rather than the whole contribution.
limitation: It is not total employer super, and it is not income. Compulsory super guarantee is excluded, so a well paid employee with no negotiated extra reads zero; and the ATO notes these contributions "aren't included in your employee's assessable income", so adding this column to gross pay to build a remuneration measure double counts nothing but overstates taxable income.
rationale: The ATO page defines exactly which employer contributions are reportable, gives the influence test that separates them from super guarantee, and states their treatment in the employee's income.
evidence_quote: Reportable employer super contributions aren't included in your employee's assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Employer Superannuation Contribution Reportable Amount - Event payment' with a dollar domain inferred from the name, so nothing said that the figure excludes compulsory super or why it is collected.

value_domain: Australian financial year (1 July to 30 June)
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Finalising your STP data
variable_description: The financial year the row belongs to, and the window that every year-to-date amount on it accumulates within before resetting on 1 July. It is also the unit the employer signs off: a finalisation declaration is "lodged by 14 July each year indicating you have fully reported for the financial year for each employee", after which the ATO pre-fills the employee's tax return. On the employment termination payment tables it still labels the year, even though ETPs are reported by payment date rather than as year-to-date totals.
value_definition: A financial year label running 1 July to 30 June. The jobs and ETP tables are named for one year each, so within those tables the column is constant.
limitation: The year follows the pay day, not the work: hours worked in late June and paid in July land in the following year, which shifts a person's apparent earnings across the boundary. A year's figures are also provisional for a long time, since the ATO allows amendment of finalised STP information "up to 5 years after the end of financial year", so an extract taken early can differ from the same year read later.
rationale: The finalisation chapter defines the financial year as the reporting and sign-off unit for STP and states the amendment window, which is what determines how stable a year's totals are.
evidence_quote: A finalisation declaration is a declaration in the approved form lodged by 14 July each year indicating you have fully reported for the financial year for each employee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Financial Year' and nothing else, with the domain inferred from the variable name, so it did not connect the year to the year-to-date reset or to finalisation.

value_domain: Reportable fringe benefits amount, section 57A exempt employer (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Fringe benefits tax - a guide for employers, chapter 5 Reportable fringe benefits
variable_description: The grossed-up value of an employee's reportable fringe benefits where the employer is exempt from fringe benefits tax under section 57A.
